iucn.long: Reassessed in 2021 as Near Threatened on the IUCN Red List (previously Least Concern), because of a suspected decline of about 30% over three generations, mainly in West Africa.

overview.text: The Ball Python, or Royal Python, is the smallest of Africa's pythons: a calm, non-venomous constrictor from West and Central Africa. Its name comes from its habit of rolling into a tight ball, with its head tucked inside, when it feels threatened. It is one of the most traded pet reptiles in the world.

size.label: Adults
size.text: Adults are usually about 0.9 to 1.5 m long; the maximum is about 1.8 m (72 in).

distribution.label: Native
distribution.text: West and Central Africa. A CITES study described its population density as high in Ghana, medium in Togo and low in Benin.

habitat.text: Grasslands, savannas and sparsely wooded country.

behaviour.text: When stressed it curls into a ball, protecting its head in the middle of its coils, instead of biting.

conservation.text: The main threat is the capture of wild snakes for the international pet trade, which a CITES study described as continuing and possibly increasing.

funfacts.text: It is named for the way it rolls up into a ball when scared.
